analysis:
The only changed code is in StandaloneServer.swift ensureMemoryHeadroomForLoad (head lines 1538-1564). Before evicting an idle cached model for load headroom, it now drops reclaimable memory once: GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments() and then MLX.Memory.clearCache(), the latter gated on nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed. The new helper is releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad (1562-1565). The poolDropped flag is initialised from GlobalKVCacheBudget.busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory() and then forces one extra loop iteration with `continue` (1546-1550). This runs at most once per call, so it cannot loop unboundedly. If memory is still short, the original eviction path or the capacityUnavailable throw follows unchanged.

Security relevance (T-028, T-041, TB-007): clearCache returns pooled MLX buffers and does not introduce new plaintext exposure. It does not touch the SSD prefix cache, the KEK, the HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping or the TTL. The attestation, authorization, wire and billing boundaries are untouched.

The clearCache call is guarded by nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed. That guard preserves the native MiMo retention invariants and avoids releasing handles during an unproven native shutdown. The surrounding stop/finishShutdown, evict and reslice code in the supplied head text is unchanged context. It already guards reclaim and clearCache with nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed.

Unverified contract: the implementation of GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments and busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory is outside the supplied evidence. I rely on the comment that it only drops free KV segments and waits briefly. Could it clear segments of in-flight requests, or block the actor for long? That is a correctness and availability question, not an observed security regression. It is a minor point for integration; I did not find any issue.
